desc:
The array nums is sorted in non-decreasing order. Rearrange it so that its elements appear in this order: the largest, the smallest, the second largest, the second smallest, the third largest, and so on, until all elements are used. Return the rearranged array.

An O(1)-extra-space solution exists: the trick is to pack two numbers into one cell.

nums = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7]
result = [7, 1, 6, 2, 5, 3, 4]
constraints: nums is sorted in non-decreasing order
hints: Two pointers, one at the start and one at the end, give the answer immediately if you may write into a new array.
To work in place, a cell must hold both its old value (still needed by later steps) and its new value.
Let m = max + 1. Store nums[i] += (new value % m) * m. The old value is cell % m and the new value is cell // m. After one pass, divide every cell by m.
editorial: With a new array this is a plain two-pointer merge: take from the right end for even output positions and from the left end for odd positions.

To avoid the extra array, encode two values in one cell. Choose m larger than every value, so any value v < m can be recovered as cell % m. At output position i, add (source % m) * m to the cell; reading the source with % m makes sure that a source cell that was already modified still yields its original value. The finished value of each cell is cell // m.
The bound 10,000 on the values keeps m * m near 108, safely inside a 32-bit integer. The algorithm makes two linear passes: O(n) time and O(1) extra space.
